headline: ALIBABA CLOSES
ITS TOP **QWEN**
cover.hook_pick_reason: The claim hook names the company and the news in plain words, and slides 1 to 4 back it fully: Qwen4-Max has closed weights, while smaller Qwen4 models are promised open. The number hooks need context to land, and the last option drops the company name. No reader-impact hook: the article states no effect on what ordinary readers pay, use or risk, and it has no price comparison with rivals.

slides.title: Alibaba keeps its top Qwen closed
body: Alibaba, China's e-commerce and cloud giant, launched **Qwen4-Max**, the new flagship of its Qwen family of AI models. It is keeping the model's weights, the files that let others run it themselves, **closed**.

slides.title: 2.4 trillion parameters
body: Qwen4-Max has **2.4 trillion parameters**, reads text, images and video, and takes up to **one million tokens** in a single prompt. Developers can use it through Alibaba's QwenCloud API.

slides.title: $1.50 in, $4.50 out
body: Access through QwenCloud costs **$1.50 per million input tokens** and **$4.50 per million output tokens**. Alibaba said that on its internal Work360 test, the average cost of a task fell versus the earlier Qwen3.8-Max from $4.43 to $1.67.

slides.title: Qwen is the open-weight giant
body: Qwen is already the **most downloaded open-weight model family** in the world, according to Bloomberg. Alibaba said smaller Qwen4 models **will get open weights**, with no date given.

slides.title: Attack data out, defense data in
body: Alibaba said it kept training data for **defensive cyber tasks**, such as finding and fixing software flaws, but **removed data** aimed at boosting attack skills.

slides.title: 48 hours on its own
body: Alibaba said Qwen4-Max worked on its own for **48 hours** to design a new coolant material for chips, which was then made and tested in a lab. The claim comes from Alibaba.

sources.title: Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max without open weights

facts.text: Alibaba has launched Qwen4-Max, the new flagship of its Qwen family of AI models, and is keeping its weights closed.
It has 2.4 trillion parameters, reads text, images and video, and can take up to one million tokens in a single prompt.
Developers can use Qwen4-Max through the QwenCloud API, at $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens.
On its internal Work360 test, the average cost of a task fell versus the earlier Qwen3.8-Max from $4.43 to $1.67.
Alibaba said it kept training data for defensive cyber tasks, such as finding and fixing software flaws, but removed data aimed at boosting attack skills.
Alibaba said Qwen4-Max worked on its own for 48 hours to design a new coolant material for chips, which was then made and tested in a lab.
Alibaba said smaller Qwen4 models will get open weights, with no date given. Qwen is already the most downloaded open-weight model family in the world, according to Bloomberg.
